phase: Phase 2 -- historical thunderstorm data acquisition (labels only)

source.name: Iowa Environmental Mesonet (IEM) ASOS/METAR archive request service
source.provider: Iowa State University, Department of Agronomy
source.underlying_observations: Routine METAR and SPECI airport surface observations for VOTV, originating from the station's own GTS-distributed reports
source.access_method: HTTP GET, comma-separated ('onlycomma') export, tz=UTC, report_type=3 (routine METAR) and report_type=4 (SPECI), data=all
source.why_this_source: The export contains a dedicated, pre-parsed observed present-weather column ('wxcodes') from which thunderstorm codes can be read directly, instead of pattern-matching free-text METAR bodies.

station.name: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport, Kerala, India
station.coordinate_source: IEM station metadata as returned in every raw row (lon=76.9500, lat=8.4667)
station.note_on_coordinates: The existing Open-Meteo dataset was fetched for 8.4855 N, 76.9492 E (a grid point ~2.1 km north of the aerodrome). The labels are station observations at the aerodrome coordinates; the offset is small relative to the hourly label resolution but must be acknowledged in Phase 3.

coverage.hourly_grid_source: exact UTC hour index of dataset/weather_data_with_code.csv (227,928 rows, 2000-01-01 00:00Z .. 2025-12-31 23:00Z)

temporal_resolution.raw: individual METAR/SPECI reports; nominal cadence is not fixed and changed over time
temporal_resolution.hour_assignment_rule: a report whose valid time t falls in [H, H+1) contributes to hour H; the label for hour H therefore describes the whole clock hour H

observed_cadence_eras.2000-2005: ~7-14 reports/day, dominated by :40 past the hour
observed_cadence_eras.2006-2011: ~14-18 reports/day, dominated by :40 and :10 past the hour

label_definition.positive_rule: thunderstorm_label = 1 for hour H when at least one valid observed report in [H, H+1) carries a TS-family present-weather code at the station (TS, TSRA, +TSRA, -TSRA, TSGR, TSDZ, TS/HZ, ...) or a vicinity code (VCTS).
label_definition.zero_rule: thunderstorm_label = 0 when hour H contains at least one valid observed report and none of them carries such a code.
label_definition.missing_rule: thunderstorm_label = NaN when hour H contains no valid observed report at all. Absence of a report is never treated as evidence of absence of a thunderstorm.
explicitly_not_used_as_label: blind regex search of raw METAR text for 'TS'
TS appearing only inside TEMPO, BECMG, NOSIG, PROBnn or other trend/forecast groups
RETS (recent thunderstorm, i.e. not occurring at observation time)

vicinity_handling.decision: VCTS is included in the primary label because IEM's wxcodes is the source's observed present-weather field, which is the condition the task allowed. The effect is negligible (single-digit records) and is isolated in the thunderstorm_label_strict column, which excludes vicinity-only reports.

derived_columns.thunderstorm_label_strict: same, but VCTS-only hours are 0 (station thunderstorm only)
derived_columns.thunderstorm_label_recovered: audit/sensitivity variant that additionally sets 1 where a malformed pre-2012 body demonstrably encoded an observed TS that IEM's wxcodes failed to parse (e.g. '5000TS', 'TS/-DZ'); never a silent replacement for the primary label
derived_columns.wxcodes_observed: distinct observed present-weather groups in the hour, for audit
derived_columns.n_reports: number of valid observed reports in the hour
derived_columns.n_reports_full_decode: reports in the hour carrying both altimeter and temperature groups
derived_columns.n_reports_with_wx: reports in the hour carrying a decodable present-weather group
derived_columns.wx_field_observed: 1 when the hour has >=1 report with a decodable present-weather group
derived_columns.n_ts_reports: number of reports in the hour carrying a TS-family code

missing_data_treatment.evidence_caveat: A report that contains no present-weather group is not evidence that no thunderstorm occurred. Hours whose only reports lack a decodable present-weather group are exposed via wx_field_observed=0 and should be excluded or masked in modelling.

report_density_and_stability.conclusion: 2000-2013 is NOT suitable for modelling. The present-weather field is absent entirely in 2000-2002 (zero decodable present-weather groups in 8,486 reports) and present in only 1.8%-64.8% of reports up to 2013, with a label rate that swings between 0.0% and 2.4% per year for reasons that track encoding practice rather than weather (e.g. 2005 = 1.66% but 2006 = 0.12%). From 2014 the present-weather coverage is >=71.6% in every year and the label rate stabilises at 3.3%-5.0%. The recommended modelling window is 2014-2025 restricted to wx_field_observed == 1; 2016-2025 is the most homogeneous sub-window.

limitations: Observations only describe the aerodrome point; a thunderstorm over the city or the catchment that is not within the station's vicinity is not labelled.
METAR present weather is a human/sensor judgement of 'thunderstorm observed at the station'; its detection range is finite and reporting practice varies between observers.
The hour label aggregates reports within [H, H+1), so it is a same-hour (nowcast-style) target, not a lead-time-shifted target. Phase 3 must apply any lead-time shift explicitly.

Pre-2012 reports use a legacy, frequently malformed encoding in which the present-weather group was sometimes glued to the visibility group ('5000TS') or written with slashes ('TS/-DZ'), causing IEM to leave wxcodes empty. 111 such observed TS reports were recovered into an audit-only column; they are not in the primary label.
~1,740 reports mention TS only in TEMPO/BECMG trend groups. These never produce a positive label. They were verified by cutting each body at the first trend marker.
The dataset is a label table only. It is deliberately NOT merged into the Open-Meteo features and no model was retrained in this phase.
IEM is a redistribution archive; no formal SLA and occasional ingestion duplicates exist (12 duplicate timestamps in Jan 2013 were de-duplicated, none conflicting).
Coverage ends 2025-12-30 23:30Z, so 2025-12-31 is entirely unobserved (NaN).

validation.run_by: dataset/build_thunderstorm_labels.py (assertions) and an independent rebuild in the same phase
validation.timestamps_parse: PASS -- all 227,928 grid timestamps parse as UTC
validation.timestamps_are_utc: PASS -- tz is UTC, source requested with tz=UTC
validation.no_duplicate_hourly_timestamps: PASS -- grid is unique and strictly increasing
validation.labels_only_0_1_nan: PASS -- all three label columns hold only 0.0, 1.0 or NaN
validation.no_future_information: PASS -- each hour label uses only reports inside that same clock hour; no forward-looking window, no trend/forecast group
validation.station_coordinates_consistent: PASS -- single station_id, single lat/lon over all rows
validation.source_field_preserved: PASS -- wxcodes_observed retains the raw observed codes per hour
validation.grid_matches_open_meteo: PASS -- identical timestamp set to weather_data_with_code.csv

phase_3_note: Ready for synchronization once the modelling window and the wx_field_observed mask are agreed. This phase intentionally did not merge labels into the ML dataset, did not retrain, and did not modify the existing model, dataset or outputs.
